text: Fog. Lanterns. Those were miners. Shoot them anyway. Shoot them anyway.
I can run forever. I have been running since thirty-nine.
A shovel. Good. Someone should dig them a proper place. Not tonight. Tonight it is for the other thing.
Mauser. Their rifle, their bullets. Tonight it does not matter whose heads.
I write down their number. Someone should. Nobody wrote down his.
My brother would like this inn. He liked any place with a fire. He would not like the windows.
Nobody stays on the floor. Not here. Not in this place.
Run, little soldier. Run while you can.
This will do. This will do.
Crawling. Like they made my brother crawl. ...Finish it.
Enough. A sniper does not drink four bottles. A sniper wants to.
A name. They had names, once. I keep them. Somebody should keep them.
The music box. Reinholt's daughter's. She had a child. I had a brother. One of us is still looking.
Round fifty. I have run out of pages. I am writing on my hand.
My eyes hurt. My hands do not care. Good hands.
Sights right, grip right. Now it only has to be honest. Nothing else here is.
Papers. Their papers. I keep everything they write. Someone has to read it, after.
Ostrowski. From Wilcza Góra. ...I know your face. I was a girl. You had a dog.
Round twenty-five. New gun, new measure. I am counting from here. Again.
Collected. Like my brother. They knew, at the end. They knew.
London is dark again. Good. Dark is good. Dark means they are lying down.

I have seen it before tonight. On the dead by the road. A glass splinter in the right hand, and it was still warm. Same hand, every time. I thought it was a wound. It is not a wound. The Russian dead do not have it. Only theirs. Somebody gave it to them.
Twelve. It is the twenty-fourth. Wigilia. Somewhere my mother is looking at the first star. She sets a plate for the one who is missing. Two plates, this year.
I will carry it. He carried enough.
A bell every time I earn. I will shoot the bell.
Sixty-two, and now they pay me twice. Nobody ever paid me once.
I could run to Kraków. There is nothing to run to in Kraków.
My rifle hums when it is empty. Everything here hums. Fine. Let it.
One more weapon. One more chance. I keep running out of chances.
Siostra Agnieszka. She was real. She nursed the laborers until they would not let her. Thank you, sister. (Sister Agnieszka.)
Jette. The label says Jette. ...She said no. Good. Somebody said no.
More. It always wants you to have more. That is how they got the laborers too. More.
Four measures. It does not wear off. One fewer thing to count.
A furnace that teaches guns. Of course they built it before bread. They always build it before bread.
Głodny, Dutch. You just told me you are a hungry woman. ...Tonight, fine. We are all hungry women.
Dziękuję. Not jen-koo-yeh. Your grandmother is weeping somewhere.
That is not a swear. You just said 'bright plague.' ...Fine. Tonight it is a swear.
Power. The laborers built that switch. Now we use it. I am sorry. We use it.
All of them. At once. If it were only so easy out there. In the east.
Everything falls in one shot. Like it should. Like it never does.
My page was neat. He has better handwriting than me. He had more time.
Thank you. You go in the notebook. The good page. It is a short page.
Burning, losing height, short of their own lines. I'm writing down the time. Somebody will want the time.
Rifle, book, pencil. I am ready. I have been ready for two years.
Those were the men who came for us. Now they come for us again. They do not know the difference.
Sześćdziesiąt... I am losing count. Good. (Sixty.)
The pilot. He's alive. Legs trapped under the panel. Write that down: Selwyn, alive. ...I am writing that down.
...Pan Ostrowski. From the end of the lane. You had a dog with one ear.
Tomek. You saw Tomek.
He wrote that. That he practised on the rats. That he still missed.
...Thank you for looking.
Then if I ever see a backwards hook, I'll know it's his.
KB... four-four-seven-one.
I'm writing it in the book. On the good page.
It's his. Tomek's. It was in the tank room. With the... with the others.
He was a terrible shot, Dutch. I used to tell him he'd starve if he had to hunt alone. And they put him in a tank.
I was too late.
...Za duszę. For the soul. You said it right. First time.
Rest easy. Nobody is selling you now. Nobody.
The bell. My brother wrote that the walls hum. This is louder than a wall.
Fire, and I am still here. Good beer.
The brandy. My eye is clear. Into the book.
The stout is still in me. Hit me. They will see.
It is counting for me. Fine. I count too. I count better.
Lightning from my rifle. I will not write how.
Three guns. More marks in the notebook.
Schnapps. Quick hands for lifting. Good.
Reload, fast. The tonic is still in my fingers.
Faster. The gun is hungry tonight. So are they.
Behind the helmet glass. Same violet. Break the glass, aim for the light.
He let go at the end. Did not fight it. I will write that he did not fight it.
A box that robs the poor. I have met that box before. It wore a uniform.
I could do more with a sharpened spoon. I have.
The drummer. The child's toy. It follows us. Everything here follows us.
Good. Finally something in this place is on our side.
Their furnace. Their glass. Our gun now. It is still their furnace.
It changed the rifle. I do not want to know how. I will not write it down.
Bottle. Here.
A gift. Nothing here is a gift. Drink anyway. Drink.
Four bells. Shoot them in order. Like counting. I can count.
Break the heart. Break all of it.
Count with me. Jeden, dwa, trzy... it helps. Cztery...
Not my rifle. But it is learning.
The soldier. He is standing. Do not look at his face. Shoot. Shoot.
Chicago Lament, twice taught. Thirty rounds. I will make them count. I always do.
East. The rail line. It goes to the salt works. I know that line.
That other voice. Cheerful. On his frequency. That was not Fasbender.
He says Gravelight. He knows the plane. Someone was waiting for us.
A man alone, calling and calling. He has been doing this a while.
Kaltenbrunn. The salt works. My brother's letters came from there.
It hums, he says. Tomasz wrote of a hum. Then he stopped writing.
The innkeeper listened to the works' channels. He wrote them down. Look for the notes.
Paper. Small, with numbers. The whole house, not just this room.
A note. Frequency and a number. I keep it.
Here. Written fast, but numbered. He knew someone would come.
First of three. I can feel it. The others are hidden the same way.
Two. The last one is close. Nothing here is far.
Three. Now the radio. One, two, three, in order. A wrong one makes noise, and noise brings them.
We have all of it. Behind the bar. I will read, someone turns.
The cabinets. Open. All of them. A gift from a voice we don't know.
Wrong. Again, from the first note. Quickly, they come.
No. The first number. Then the second. They heard that.
The transfer lists said Thalbach. Two hundred names. I am going to find where they put them.
Engines sold. Routes written. Crews 'provided'. Everything here was bought from someone.
A waypoint in a desert. They were never coming back.
A model. Hers, I think. Jette. The label says Jette.
'Nein.' She said no. Good.
Sixty-one. Sixty-two. ...That thing has no number. I don't have a number for that.
Old door's buried. New hole, west side. Move.
Twenty. In the wind. ...Good. Good.
No crew. Buckled harnesses. ...They were taken OUT. Like Tomek. Like all of them.
Count with me. Thirty seconds. Dwadzieścia dziewięć, dwadzieścia osiem...
Hole in the wing. Good. It's a window.
Empty, I bet. Like this one. Flying for nobody.
Two of the racks are marked. The hook. They're duds. They MADE them duds. Thank you. Thank you, whoever you are.
...That one's gone. I'm sorry. I'm sorry.
Riedl. Haas. Pohl. I'm writing them back in. In ink this time.
'Riedl, A.' ...I'll keep it.
Three names. They had names. I have them now.
I am not writing that one down.
A desert. I've never seen one. It's like the salt. It's exactly like the salt.
It walks through the wall. It walks through the WALL. I can't count it. I have to count it.
They're in suits. They put them in suits and glass. Who DOES that.
I told you at the pens. I told you I'd seen it. ...You should have said, Peg. You should have just said.
Sowa said you can hit anything if you've already hit it in your head. I've never hit the Moon in my head.
In the air. I'll take him in the air. ...There.
'Nobody cancels.' ...We'll see.
For Tomasz. For Agnieszka. For two hundred names. ...No.
I'll read it. I read everything. Somebody has to.
Look at the Earth. The violet. It is pulling back.
It is spreading over the Earth. Every round, a little more. Every round, more of them get up.
Sixty-three. ...and one.
I can see the whole yard from up here. Two hundred metres. ...Easy. Too easy.
She sold them the engines. She sold the inn its coffins. She sold the sickness its glass. ...Sixty-two. I'm counting you.
...I can't count any higher. Why can't I count.
A crack. Twelve kilometres, maybe more. I can't count that. ...I'll write 'one'.
'Riedl.' Here. He's here.
'Haas.' ...Here.
All three. They flew them here. In their harnesses. ...I have their names. That's what I can do. It's the only thing I can do.
Same hand. Every time.
The splinter. Hit it and they fall like men again.
Above the eye, that one. They put it there. So did I.
They dosed him to see when he would die. He would not die. ...I know this file. I have seen this kind of file. In two languages.
The back of his neck, when he turns. The line goes in there.
Paul. ...Not a mark. A name.
Peg will be jealous. Or she already drank three. Good for her.
Bitter. Good. Now I see where they hide things. They hide everything.
It shows me the clock on every gift. Nothing here is free. I knew that. I have always known that.
I hate that this works. I hate it.
Sniper brandy, from the men who hunted us. My hands are steadier. Damn them. Damn them for being right about my hands.
Bavarian beer. Thick. Good. I need to be thick tonight.
Cold, cheap, and it counts. Like the man who made it. Like me.
A thief's bird. ...The only one that comes back. I read the label. I read everything. It is how I am still alive.
Static in the blood. My brother would have laughed at this. Then he would have been frightened. Then he would have laughed again.
Not yet. Not today. Not here.
She made this to keep them alive. They used it to keep them working. I drink it to keep us alive. That is the only difference I have.
Bubbles. ...I do not like my feet off the ground. I will make an exception. One.
The owl on the glass. Somebody here was on our side.
This one's mine for good. I'm writing that down so I believe it.
Fizz. Fast hands. Faster than theirs. That is all I ask for.
Bitter. Yes.
They wrote down who made it. They never write down who it was made from.
Finished. Reload. Do not relax. They do not.
Quiet. It will not last. It never does. Nothing does.
They come. Count them.
Again. Good. I have pages left. I have pages left.
He stops when I stop. He turns when I turn. ...Good. I can count on him.
He wrote everything down. Every hour. ...I understand him. I do not want to understand him.
Kaltenbrunn. Six kilometres from home. Good. Then I know the way out. If there is one.
Shoot them. They would want it. I would want it. Promise me you would.
Keep them coming. The notebook is never full. That is the trouble with it.

'Conditions of use. Skyhook Sekt. One. Lift is provided. Landing is the Holder's responsibility. Two. The formula was made drinkable by a technician who would not fly the aircraft it was made for. The undersigned wishes it recorded that this is not the same as not wanting to. Three. A customer who can leave the ground has not yet left the Plan. Four. The second jump is a courtesy. There is no third. Five. These pass. The landing does not. Six. Cancellation. Land.' Signed, Vendelin. ...I'm writing that down.

'Conditions of use. Magpie Mead. One. Recovery is not refund. Two. The Provider does not sell this Plan to persons who already own a yard. It sells it to persons who think they do. Three. The magpie is a thief. It is also the only bird that comes back. Four. Nothing on the range goes to waste. Five. Thrift. A habit of looking down. Six. Cancellation. Leave it where it lies. The Product will not stop you. Nothing here will.' Signed, Vendelin. Under it: 'Read this.' ...I always do.

'Conditions of use. Fine Print Fernet. Six. Cancellation. You may refuse any Plan by not inserting a token. This is the only cancellation procedure the undersigned has ever been able to guarantee. It works every time it is tried. It is almost never tried.' Signed, Vendelin. ...Sixty-two tries.
Line and hook. I was taught the same with a rifle.
A terrible shot. A good laugh.
He would have liked you. He liked everyone. It was his only flaw.
Is that about me?
Finish it. Then never sing it again.
In church. Before.
Głodny. You are a man.
God help Poland.
Every one.
It was Germans. Now it is Germans, and villagers, and Russians in greatcoats. The ink does not care. I am starting to.
Dziękuję. You thank me like a man chewing gravel.
Then Babcia chewed gravel.
I know.
Neither is lying. Unlike SOE.
When this is done, I will still be Polish, and the Russians will be in Warsaw. London will not fix either.
Thirty-two. You missed the one in the fog.
You talk to the machines.
Do they talk back?
Your machine. Hattie. She is loud.
Then I am very alive tonight.
Your grandmother. Where was she from?
...Six kilometers from here.
How many tonight?
Thirty-one. I count for you.
You did not come for Fasbender.
That is not an answer.
Your orders. Do they say to bring us out?
I asked about us.
Few rounds left. Few.
Empty. Do diabła. (To the devil.)
Window closed.
Ammunition. The only thing here worth the price.
Peg's kind of gun. I will borrow her taste. And her nerve.
Heavy. Loud. Everything I am not. Everything I need to be tonight.
A pistol. For when they are close. They are always close now.
Gewehr. Semi-automatic. Good. I am tired of working the bolt.
Shotgun. For people who cannot aim. My hands are shaking. So. Today, me.
Machine pistol. Ugly. It does not have to be pretty. It has to be close.
Fasbender's toy. Built in the same mine as my brother's grave. I will use it anyway.
I drink. Fine.
I bring it.
I follow.
I hold. They come, I count them.
The door. Yes.
Boards. Yes.
I save.
Yes. We run them.
Go. I watch.
Crate moved.
No current. The machine sleeps. Let it.
Too little Scrip. Later. If there is a later.
Open. I know what is behind this one. I wish I did not.
Yes. I do it.
I carry it. Cover me.
I find them. You hold the windows.
I bring them.
I stand here. Nobody passes.
I do the machine.
Good. Send them here.
I see it. One shot.
My key. Tell me when.
No. Not now.
Not found yet. Show me.
We do not know it yet. I do not guess. Guessing is how you die here.
This can go wrong. You say, I do.
You are busy. I do the last one.
Done.
Ready. The last one is yours.
Wait. Fight first.
This is yours. I watch.
One more.
Again. Good.
Back to it.
Now again.
You must be here for this.
Jeden. (One.)
Clean. Into the book.
That is how it is done, Dutch.
Yes.
I go.
I buy it. My Scrip.
Yes. I buy.
I hold there.
I buy one for you.
I go there.
Coming.
Now I have enough. I go.
Done.
Full again.
Pistol is better now.
Blastproof. Good.
Crate. We see.
In the fire. Cover me.
Door is open.
Bought.
Hawkeye. Now I see everything.
Ironhide. Good.
Marathon Malt. I run.
Overclock. It burns.
Packmule. One more rifle.
Second Wind. I lift you faster.
Trap is on.
Trigger Tonic. Fast hands.
Twin Barrel. Two.
No. Cannot.
No more bottles.
My guns are better. No.
I have it.
No power.
No way there.
Power. On.
Not enough. I stop. I stop.
At your feet. Take.
For you. Take it from me.
Back to it.
Again. Back to it.
Not enough Scrip. Wait.
Need 100 more. I earn it.
Need 1,000 more. I earn it.
Need 1,250 more. I earn it.
Need 1,500 more. I earn it.
Need 200 more. I earn it.

Need 2,500 more. I earn it.

Need 4,000 more. I earn it.
Need 500 more. I earn it.
Need 5,000 more. I earn it.
Need 600 more. I earn it.
Need 700 more. I earn it.

Need 900 more. I earn it.
Too much. I earn it slowly.
Blackout. Here.
Clearance. The crate is cheap.
Death's Door. Here.
Double Scrip. Here.
Fortify. Here.
Resupply. Here.
There. Something fell. Take it.
The crate is cheap. Move.
Double. My notebook will need more pages. I did not bring more pages.
Windows closed. Do not waste it. Breathe.
Ammunition. Count it later. Shoot now.
Empty. One moment. One.
Get up. I am not losing anyone else here. Get up.
Up. Shoot. Cry later. I will too.
I've got you. Hold on. Hold on. Look at me, not at them.
One hundred. I write it down.
One hundred fifty.
Two hundred. For my brother.
Twenty-five.
Three hundred. Still counting. Somebody has to.
Fifty. I am counting.
The lever. Stand back, or lie down with them.
Board's up!
Jakub. ...He breathes. Leave him. He has walked out of worse places than this. He will walk out of this.
Reloading!
No violet light this time. Only flak. ...That is almost a comfort. Almost.
The book! Shoot the book out of his hands!
I'm down. Quickly. Quickly, or I get up wrong.
Tomek... I'm sorry. I came too late.
Big one. Coming now.
The overseer. Obersteiger. My brother worked under him. Let me. Let me.
The drill core. Aim there. I want him to know whose sister did it.
Russians. Hundreds. Walking into German guns and the guns are not firing. ...Nothing about this is right.
Glass body. Head only. It is all I aim for anyway.
Upstairs. The civilian is turning. Do not wait for them to look at you. You will not shoot if they look at you.
Bad place. Stay away. I have seen what is there.
Not there. Danger.
The nurse. Kill her. Kill her now, before she calls them!
Behind you. Fast.
You are down. Stay down, shoot low. I come. I come!
One of us is on the floor. Cover me. Nobody stays on the floor here.
Window. Open. There.
